Form pluperfect (-eram) and future perfect (-ero) from the perfect stem
Translate perfect forms with the German Präteritum and the future perfect idiomatically (Si veneris… = Wenn du kommst…)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} work out that 'vicerat' comes from 'vincere' and translate it as 'er hatte gesiegt'?

prerequisites.reason: The perfect stem is learnt in contrast to the present stem
German past tense forms are the translation targets
The concept of past time is known
Anteriority is known from the German Plusquamperfekt

topics.laenderNotes: Bayern teaches all indicative active tenses including future perfect in Jgst. 6 (Latin from Jgst. 6); BW leaves the future perfect to Kl. 9/10 and NRW does not name it.

topics.subject: Latein
topics.name: Demonstrative Pronouns
topics.description: Decline and translate the demonstratives is/ea/id, hic, ille, ipse and idem with their pronominal genitive and dative (-ius, -i), and use them to follow who is meant across sentences.
evidence: Recognise forms of is, hic, ille, ipse and idem including eius, huius, illius
Translate them as pronoun or as determiner as the context requires
Use demonstratives to track references between sentences in a text
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain who 'ille' and 'hic' refer to in a sentence about Caesar and Pompey?

prerequisites.reason: Builds on pronoun forms and their functions
Shared endings must be kept apart

topics.laenderNotes: is and qui come in the first year; hic, ille, ipse in Bayern Jgst. 7, iste and idem in BW only in Kl. 9/10.

topics.subject: Latein
topics.name: Fourth and Fifth Declension
topics.description: Decline the nouns of the u-declension (senatus, manus, domus) and e-declension (res, dies, spes) and translate the many meanings of res in fixed expressions (res publica, res gestae).
evidence: Decline u- and e-declension nouns in all cases
Distinguish forms such as senatus (nom./gen.) by context
Translate res in phrases like res publica, res adversae and res gestae
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} translate 'res publica' and 'res gestae' and say which declension 'res' belongs to?

prerequisites.reason: Completes the declension system

topics.laenderNotes: Bayern Jgst. 7; BW Kl. 9/10, NRW second stage, Niedersachsen by Kl. 9.

topics.subject: Latein
topics.name: The Passive Voice
topics.description: Form the passive in the present system (laudor, laudabar, laudabor) and the perfect system with the perfect participle plus esse (laudatus est), and translate it with German werden-passive or an active paraphrase.
evidence: Form passive forms of all tenses
Recognise the PPP with esse as a perfect passive and make it agree with the subject
Translate the passive with the agent (a/ab + ablative) and as an active sentence where natural
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} translate 'Urbs a Romanis capta est' and say why 'capta' has a feminine ending?

prerequisites.reason: Passive endings attach to the same tense stems
The perfect passive uses the fourth principal part

osMatches.note: os: active and passive voice in English

topics.laenderNotes: Bayern Jgst. 7, BW Kl. 6–8, NRW first stage, Niedersachsen by Kl. 9.

topics.subject: Latein
topics.name: Comparison and Adverbs
topics.description: Form and translate comparatives (-ior) and superlatives (-issimus, -errimus, -illimus) including the irregular ones (bonus – melior – optimus), the ablative of comparison and quam, and adverbs in -e and -(i)ter.
evidence: Form regular and irregular comparatives and superlatives
Translate the elative superlative (sehr…) and comparison with quam or the ablative
Form adverbs from adjectives and recognise their comparison
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} translate 'Nihil est melius amicitia' and explain the ablative in it?

prerequisites.reason: Comparatives follow the third declension
Comparison is known from German

topics.laenderNotes: Bayern Jgst. 8, NRW second stage (Komparation), BW Kl. 9/10 (adverbs) and Kl. 11 (comparison).

topics.subject: Latein
topics.name: Irregular Verbs
topics.nameDe: Unregelmäßige Verben (posse, ire, ferre, velle, nolle, fieri)
topics.description: Recognise and translate the irregular verbs posse, ire, ferre, velle/nolle/malle and fieri and their many compounds (abire, transire, afferre, conferre).
evidence: Conjugate posse and ire and recognise their compounds
Recognise forms of ferre including tuli and latum and its compounds
Translate forms of velle, nolle and fieri in context
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} work out that 'rettulit' belongs to 'referre' and translate it?

prerequisites.reason: Irregular principal parts must be learnt against the regular system
Compounds are analysed into prefix and stem

topics.subject: Latein
topics.name: Subjunctive Forms
topics.description: Form and recognise the four subjunctive tenses in active and passive (laudet, laudaret, laudaverit, laudavisset) and tell them apart from similar indicative forms.
evidence: Form the subjunctive of all four tenses in active and passive
Distinguish subjunctive from indicative forms (laudet / laudat, regat / reget)
Identify tense and mood of a verb form in a subordinate clause
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell you which tense and mood 'venisset' is and how it differs from 'venit'?

prerequisites.reason: Subjunctive forms exist in both voices
Subjunctive perfect forms resemble the future perfect and are built on the perfect stem

topics.laenderNotes: Bayern Jgst. 7 (all four tenses); NRW: imperfect and pluperfect subjunctive in the first stage, present and perfect in the second; BW Kl. 9/10.

topics.subject: Latein
topics.name: Deponent Verbs
topics.description: Recognise deponent verbs (hortari, vereri, loqui, sequi, pati), which have passive forms but active meaning, and semideponents (audere, gaudere), and translate their participles correctly (secutus = gefolgt, nachdem er gefolgt war).
evidence: Recognise deponents from their learning form (hortor, hortatus sum)
Translate deponent forms actively
Translate perfect participles of deponents with active meaning
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} translate 'Milites ducem secuti sunt' and explain why the passive form is translated actively?

prerequisites.reason: Deponents use the passive forms
Deponent participles behave specially in participle constructions

topics.laenderNotes: Bayern Jgst. 8 (with semideponents), BW Kl. 9/10 (semideponents Kl. 11), NRW second stage, Niedersachsen by Kl. 10.

topics.subject: Latein
topics.name: Sentence Elements in Latin
topics.description: Identify the sentence elements of Latin sentences (Prädikat, Subjekt, Prädikatsnomen, Objekte, Adverbiale, Attribute) by their form, starting from the predicate, and see that the subject can be contained in the verb ending.
evidence: Find the predicate first and determine the subject from its ending
Identify objects and adverbials by case and preposition
Mark the sentence elements of a Latin sentence and translate it
topics.assessmentPrompt: In 'Mercator in foro servis cibum dat', can {{name}} name each sentence element and say how they recognised it?

prerequisites.reason: Subject and predicate are known from German grammar
Dative and accusative objects are known from German
Identifying sentence elements is practised in German

topics.subject: Latein
topics.name: Functions of the Ablative
topics.nameDe: Ablativfunktionen (instrumenti, loci, temporis, separativus, modi, causae)
topics.description: Understand the ablative, a case German does not have, and translate its main functions with a suitable German preposition: means (mit, durch), place (in, auf), time (an, in), separation (von, aus), manner and cause, with and without a Latin preposition.
evidence: Name the function of an ablative by asking Womit?, Wo?, Wann?, Wovon?, Wie? or Warum?
Choose a fitting German preposition to translate it
Distinguish prepositions governing ablative from those governing accusative
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} translate 'Prima luce Romani gladiis pugnabant' and say which ablative functions appear?

prerequisites.reason: Ablative forms must be recognised
Ablative functions correspond to German adverbials
German prepositions are the translation tools

topics.subject: Latein
topics.name: Subordinate Clauses with the Indicative
topics.nameDe: Gliedsätze im Indikativ (dum, postquam, quod, si, quamquam)
topics.description: Recognise subordinate clauses introduced by conjunctions with the indicative (temporal: dum, ubi, postquam; causal: quod, quia; conditional: si, nisi; concessive: quamquam) and translate the sentence structure.
evidence: Mark main and subordinate clauses in a Latin sentence
Translate common subordinating conjunctions with their meaning
Translate dum with the present as 'während' in a past context
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} split 'Postquam Caesar venit, hostes fugerunt' into main and subordinate clause and translate it?

prerequisites.reason: Sentence analysis is extended to complex sentences
Main and subordinate clauses are known from German
Conjunctions are a known word class

topics.subject: Latein
topics.name: Accusative with Infinitive
topics.description: Recognise the AcI after verbs of saying, thinking and perceiving and translate it with a German dass-clause, using the infinitive to show the time relation (gleichzeitig, vorzeitig, nachzeitig) and se/suus for reference to the subject; later also the NcI (dicitur esse).
evidence: Find the signal verb, the accusative subject and the infinitive of an AcI
Translate present, perfect and future infinitives with the right time relation
Translate se in an AcI as referring to the subject of the main clause
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} translate 'Marcus dicit se amicum vidisse' as 'Marcus sagt, dass er den Freund gesehen habe'?

prerequisites.reason: Infinitives must be recognised
The AcI is analysed as an object of the predicate
It is translated with a German dass-clause

topics.laenderNotes: Active AcI in the first year (Bayern Jgst. 6), passive and future infinitives later (Bayern Jgst. 7–8); the NcI comes in Bayern Jgst. 8 and in BW only in Kl. 11.

topics.subject: Latein
topics.name: Relative Clauses and Relative Linking
topics.description: Decline qui, quae, quod, find the antecedent by gender and number, translate relative clauses, and recognise the relative connection at the start of a sentence (Quae cum ita sint…), translated with a demonstrative.
evidence: Find the antecedent of a relative pronoun by gender and number
Translate relative clauses, including ones with the antecedent left out
Translate a relative connection with dieser/diese/dieses
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} translate 'Quod ubi Caesar audivit…' correctly as 'Als Caesar dies hörte…'?

prerequisites.reason: Relative clauses are a type of subordinate clause
The relative pronoun mixes declension patterns
Relative clauses are known from German

topics.laenderNotes: Bayern treats the relative clause and the relative connection in Jgst. 6; BW Kl. 6–8.

topics.subject: Latein
topics.name: Functions of the Genitive and Dative
topics.description: Recognise and translate the main functions of the genitive (possessivus, partitivus, subiectivus/obiectivus, qualitatis, pretii) and the dative (possessivus, commodi, finalis, double dative), which often need a free German rendering.
evidence: Name the function of a genitive or dative in a sentence
Translate the dativus possessivus (Mihi liber est = ich habe ein Buch)
Distinguish genitivus subiectivus and obiectivus (amor patris) by context
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} translate 'Caesari magnus exercitus erat' as 'Caesar hatte ein großes Heer' and explain the dative?

prerequisites.reason: Case functions were first studied with the ablative
Genitive and dative forms of all declensions are needed

topics.subject: Latein
topics.name: Participium Coniunctum
topics.nameDe: Participium coniunctum (PPP, PPA) und seine Übersetzungsmöglichkeiten
topics.description: Form and recognise the perfect passive participle (PPP) and present active participle (PPA), find the noun they agree with, express the time relation (vorzeitig/gleichzeitig) and translate them as relative clause, adverbial clause, coordinated main clause or prepositional phrase.
evidence: Find the noun a participle agrees with by KNG
State the time relation and choose a fitting meaning (temporal, causal, concessive)
Translate one participle in three ways and choose the most idiomatic
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} translate 'Hostes victi fugerunt' in at least two ways, e.g. 'Die besiegten Feinde flohen' and 'Nachdem die Feinde besiegt worden waren, flohen sie'?

prerequisites.reason: The PPP is first met in the perfect passive
Participles agree like adjectives
Adverbial clauses are a translation option

topics.laenderNotes: Bayern Jgst. 7, BW Kl. 6–8, NRW first stage (Kl. 8 for Latin from Kl. 7), Niedersachsen by Kl. 9.

topics.subject: Latein
topics.name: Ablative Absolute
topics.description: Recognise the ablative absolute (noun + participle in the ablative, grammatically independent of the main clause), including the nominal form (Cicerone consule), and translate it with a subordinate clause or prepositional phrase showing the time relation and logical link.
evidence: Identify an ablative absolute and show that it is not part of the main clause
Translate it with a temporal, causal or concessive clause and with a prepositional phrase
Translate nominal ablatives absolute (Augusto imperatore = unter Kaiser Augustus)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} translate 'Urbe capta Romani domum redierunt' with a nachdem-clause and also as 'Nach der Einnahme der Stadt…'?

prerequisites.reason: The ablative absolute is a special participle construction
It builds on ablative forms and functions

topics.laenderNotes: Bayern already in Jgst. 7 with the participium coniunctum; BW Kl. 9/10, NRW second stage (Kl. 10 in the official sample plan), Niedersachsen by Kl. 9.

topics.subject: Latein
topics.name: Subjunctive in Subordinate Clauses
topics.description: Translate subordinate clauses with the subjunctive: final and consecutive ut/ne clauses, ut/ne after verbs of asking and fearing, and the cum clauses (cum narrativum, causale, concessivum), choosing the German conjunction from the context.
evidence: Distinguish final and consecutive ut-clauses (signal words such as tam, ita, tantus)
Translate cum + subjunctive as 'als', 'weil' or 'obwohl' according to context
Translate ne after verbs of fearing correctly ('dass')
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why 'Cum Caesar venisset, hostes fugerunt' is translated with 'Als' and not with 'Wenn'?

prerequisites.reason: Subjunctive forms must be recognised
Builds on indicative subordinate clauses

topics.laenderNotes: Bayern Jgst. 7, NRW first stage (final and consecutive clauses), BW Kl. 9/10, Niedersachsen by Kl. 9.

topics.subject: Latein
topics.name: Sequence of Tenses and Indirect Questions
topics.description: Use the consecutio temporum, the rule linking the subjunctive tense in a subordinate clause to the main-clause tense and the time relation, to translate subjunctive clauses correctly, especially indirect questions (Quaero, quid facias / fecisses).
evidence: Determine the time relation (gleichzeitig, vorzeitig, nachzeitig) from the subjunctive tense
Translate indirect questions with the right German tense
Explain the rule with a table of primary and historic sequence
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why 'Rogavit, quid fecissem' means 'Er fragte, was ich getan hätte' and not 'was ich tue'?

prerequisites.reason: The rule governs subjunctive subordinate clauses
Time relations were first learnt with infinitives

topics.laenderNotes: Named explicitly only in Bayern (Jgst. 7, with indirect questions); BW and NRW treat time relations in subjunctive clauses without the term.

topics.subject: Latein
topics.name: Subjunctive in Main Clauses and Conditionals
topics.nameDe: Konjunktiv im Hauptsatz und Konditionalsätze (Realis, Potentialis, Irrealis)
topics.description: Translate the independent subjunctive by its meaning (hortative, jussive, optative, deliberative, potential) and conditional sentences as real, potential or unreal (Si hoc dicas, erres; Si hoc dixisses, errasses).
evidence: Name and translate hortative, jussive and optative subjunctives (Gaudeamus! Utinam veniat!)
Classify conditional sentences as realis, potentialis or irrealis
Translate the irrealis of the present and past with the German Konjunktiv II
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} translate 'Si tacuisses, philosophus mansisses' and explain why it is an irrealis?

prerequisites.reason: Subjunctive forms must be recognised
si-clauses were first met with the indicative

externalPrerequisites.subject: Deutsch
externalPrerequisites.concept: Konjunktiv II und würde-Form für Irreales
externalPrerequisites.reason: The German translation of the irrealis needs the Konjunktiv II

osMatches.note: os: verb moods in English

topics.laenderNotes: Bayern: irrealis Jgst. 7, hortative, jussive, optative etc. Jgst. 8; BW: irrealis, hortative, jussive Kl. 9/10, other uses Kl. 11; NRW: irrealis first stage, main-clause subjunctive second stage.

topics.subject: Latein
topics.name: Gerund and Attributive Gerundive
topics.description: Recognise the nd-forms and translate the gerund as a verbal noun (ars scribendi = die Kunst des Schreibens) and the gerundive used instead of it (ad urbem capiendam = um die Stadt einzunehmen), especially with ad, causa and in.
evidence: Distinguish gerund (no noun) and gerundive (agrees with a noun)
Translate ad + nd-form and causa + nd-form as purpose ('um zu', 'zum')
Translate nd-forms with a German nominalised infinitive or a zu-infinitive
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} translate 'Caesar ad bellum gerendum profectus est' and explain which nd-form it is?

prerequisites.reason: nd-forms are learnt alongside the other verbal adjectives
Gerund cases have case functions

topics.laenderNotes: Bayern Jgst. 8, BW Kl. 9/10, NRW second stage (Kl. 10 in the sample plan), Niedersachsen by Kl. 9.

topics.subject: Latein
topics.name: Predicative Gerundive of Obligation
topics.description: Translate the gerundive with esse that expresses necessity (Carthago delenda est = Karthago muss zerstört werden), with the dative of agent and in negation (non … est = darf nicht).
evidence: Recognise gerundive + esse as an expression of obligation
Translate it with 'müssen' (passive) or 'man muss' and with the dativus auctoris
Translate the negated form with 'nicht dürfen'
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} translate 'Nobis patria defendenda est' as 'Wir müssen die Heimat verteidigen'?

prerequisites.reason: The gerundive forms are learnt first
The agent appears in the dative

topics.laenderNotes: Bayern Jgst. 8 (with the dativus auctoris), Niedersachsen by Kl. 10, BW Kl. 9/10.

topics.subject: Latein
topics.name: Indirect Speech in Latin Texts
topics.description: Recognise and translate longer passages of indirect speech, as in Caesar: statements as AcI, commands and questions in the subjunctive, subordinate clauses in the subjunctive by consecutio temporum, and se/suus for the speaker; render them with the German Konjunktiv I.
evidence: Identify where indirect speech begins and ends in a text
Translate its statements, commands and subordinate clauses correctly
Render it in German with the Konjunktiv I and resolve pronoun references
topics.assessmentPrompt: Given a short speech of Ariovistus in Caesar's indirect speech, can {{name}} translate it with German Konjunktiv I and say who 'sui' refers to?

prerequisites.reason: Statements in indirect speech are AcI constructions
Subordinate clauses follow the sequence of tenses

externalPrerequisites.subject: Deutsch
externalPrerequisites.reason: German indirect speech is the translation target

osMatches.note: os: quoted and reported speech in English

topics.laenderNotes: Bayern Jgst. 9 with the Caesar reading; BW only in Kl. 11; Niedersachsen by Kl. 10; NRW does not name it.

topics.subject: Latein
topics.name: Methods for Decoding Latin Sentences
topics.description: Decode Latin sentences systematically before translating: start from the predicate and its subject (Konstruktionsmethode), move back and forth along the sentence (Pendelmethode), read linearly while keeping open questions, or lay out clauses graphically (Einrück- or Kästchenmethode).
evidence: Mark predicates, subordinate clauses and constructions before translating
Lay out a complex sentence with the indentation or box method
Explain which decoding method they used and why
topics.assessmentPrompt: Given a long Latin sentence, does {{name}} first mark the predicates and clauses before starting to translate?

prerequisites.reason: Decoding is based on identifying sentence elements
Complex sentences need clause analysis

topics.subject: Latein
topics.name: Pre-Reading a Latin Text
topics.nameDe: Texterschließung vor der Übersetzung (Sachfelder, Tempusrelief, Konnektoren)
topics.description: Grasp a Latin text as a whole before translating it: use title and introduction, word and subject fields, persons and places, connectors, and the change of tenses (Tempusrelief) to form a hypothesis about content and structure, then check it while translating.
evidence: Collect word fields and persons from a Latin text and predict its topic
Use the tense relief to distinguish background (imperfect) from main action (perfect)
Divide a text into sections using connectors and changes of subject
topics.assessmentPrompt: Before translating a new Latin story, can {{name}} say from the words and tenses who is involved and what roughly happens?

prerequisites.reason: Text-level methods extend sentence-level decoding
The tense relief requires recognising perfect and imperfect
Reading strategies for texts are known from Deutsch

topics.subject: Latein
topics.name: Translating into Good German
topics.description: Turn a correct literal understanding into an appropriate German translation: choose tenses, resolve participles and nd-forms, adjust word order and idioms, and check and revise the translation with grammatical terminology.
evidence: Produce a translation that is both faithful to the Latin and good German
Explain the difference between a literal and a free rendering of a passage
Analyse and correct errors in their own or a classmate’s translation using grammatical terms
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} turn a literal translation of a Caesar sentence full of participles into natural German without changing its meaning?

prerequisites.reason: A correct analysis comes before a stylistically good translation
Participles are the main challenge of idiomatic translation
Good translation rests on comparing Latin and German structure

topics.laenderNotes: NRW already compares different translations of a text in the first Sek I stage; BW does so from Kl. 11.

topics.subject: Latein
topics.name: Stylistic Devices in Latin Texts
topics.nameDe: Stilmittel erkennen und ihre Funktion deuten
topics.description: Identify the main stylistic devices of Latin literature (alliteration, anaphora, asyndeton, polysyndeton, chiasm, parallelism, hyperbaton, tricolon, climax, rhetorical question, metaphor, litotes) and explain how they support the message of the passage.
evidence: Name and locate stylistic devices in a Latin passage
Explain the effect of a device in context, not just name it
Use the Latin/Greek technical terms correctly
topics.assessmentPrompt: In Caesar's 'Veni, vidi, vici', can {{name}} name the devices (asyndeton, tricolon, alliteration) and explain their effect?

prerequisites.reason: Devices are found while studying a text as a whole
Hyperbaton and chiasm are seen through KNG agreement

externalPrerequisites.subject: Deutsch
externalPrerequisites.concept: rhetorische Stilmittel in Gedichten und Reden erkennen und deuten
externalPrerequisites.reason: Many devices are first met in German literature lessons

osMatches.note: os: literary and rhetorical devices in English writing

topics.subject: Latein
topics.name: Scanning the Dactylic Hexameter
topics.description: Scan and read aloud the dactylic hexameter of Ovid and Vergil: determine syllable length (by nature and by position), mark dactyls and spondees, handle elision and the caesura, and notice how rhythm underlines meaning.
evidence: Determine long and short syllables by the rules of quantity
Mark the six feet, the elisions and the main caesura of a hexameter
Read a few hexameters aloud with metrical stress and comment on a rhythmic effect
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} scan the first line of Ovid's Metamorphoses and read it aloud in rhythm?

prerequisites.reason: Metre builds on vowel length and stress
Verse and rhythm are basic poetry terms from Deutsch

externalPrerequisites.subject: Deutsch
externalPrerequisites.reason: Metrical feet are introduced in German poetry analysis

topics.laenderNotes: Bayern introduces the hexameter with Ovid in Jgst. 11 (after the elegiac couplet with Martial in Jgst. 9–10); NRW asks for metrical recital in the second Sek I stage; BW only in Kl. 12/13.

topics.subject: Latein
topics.name: The Elegiac Couplet
topics.description: Scan the elegiac couplet of hexameter and pentameter used by Ovid (Amores, Ars amatoria), Catullus and Martial, recognising the pentameter's two halves and the typical sense units of each couplet.
evidence: Scan a pentameter with its fixed central break
Recognise the couplet structure as a unit of meaning
Explain how the form suits epigram and love elegy
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} scan an epigram of Martial and show where the pentameter breaks into two halves?

prerequisites.reason: The couplet starts with a hexameter

topics.laenderNotes: Bayern meets the elegiac couplet first, with Martial in Jgst. 9 and Catullus/Ovid in Jgst. 10.

topics.subject: Latein
topics.name: Latinum-Level Translation
topics.description: Translate an unseen original prose text of medium difficulty (e.g. Caesar, Cicero, Livy) into correct, appropriate German with a dictionary, at the level certified by the Latinum, which many university courses require.
evidence: Translate an unseen passage of about 150–180 words of original prose within the set time
Render all major constructions (AcI, participles, nd-forms, subjunctive clauses) correctly
Answer interpretation questions on content and structure of the passage
topics.assessmentPrompt: Given an unseen Cicero passage and a dictionary, can {{name}} produce a correct German translation in 90 minutes?

prerequisites.reason: The Latinum requires correct and appropriate translation
Original prose contains indirect speech
The dictionary is used for unseen texts

topics.laenderNotes: Länder fix when the Latinum is awarded (KMK 2005: at least ausreichend in the decisive report). Bayern: Jahreszeugnis of Jgst. 10 or 11 (a Kleines Latinum after Jgst. 9). NRW G9: end of the Einführungsphase for Latin from Kl. 7, end of Kl. 10 for Latin from Kl. 5, end of Q1 for Latin from Kl. 9. Niedersachsen: Latinum at the end of Kl. 11 (Kleines Latinum at the end of Kl. 10). Hessen: end of the Einführungsphase for Latin as second foreign language. Berlin: after Jg. 10 (Latin from Kl. 5) or the 2nd Kurshalbjahr (from Kl. 7). Otherwise an Ergänzungsprüfung is possible.

topics.subject: Latein
topics.name: Interpreting Latin Texts
topics.description: Interpret Latin texts in the Oberstufe: analyse structure, key terms and stylistic and metrical features, relate the text to its author, genre and historical context, compare it with other texts or reception documents and reach a reasoned judgement.
evidence: Show how structure, key terms and devices express the text's message, with Latin quotations
Place a text in its historical and literary context
Compare a Latin text with a modern text or image on the same theme and evaluate both
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain, with Latin quotations, how a Seneca letter tries to convince its reader?

prerequisites.reason: Interpretation explains the function of language features
Interpretation rests on a secure translation

topics.subject: Latein
topics.name: Transition to Original Texts
topics.description: Move from textbook Latin to original literature with adapted or easy original texts, such as Phaedrus' fables, Martial's epigrams, medieval texts (Gesta Romanorum, Carmina Burana) or Pliny's letters, getting used to authentic style and to annotated editions.
evidence: Translate an annotated original text using the notes and a dictionary
Explain the point (Pointe) of a fable or epigram
Describe features of the genre (fable, epigram, letter)
topics.assessmentPrompt: After translating a fable of Phaedrus, can {{name}} explain its moral and how the animals stand for people?

prerequisites.reason: Original texts require text-level reading strategies
Original texts use the full set of participle constructions
The fable genre is known from Deutsch

topics.laenderNotes: Bayern at the start of Jgst. 9 (Phaedrus, Hygin, Gellius, Vulgata); NRW original texts by the end of the 3rd year; BW moves to original texts in the first half of Kl. 10 for Latin as second foreign language.

topics.subject: Latein
topics.name: Nepos: Lives of Famous Men
topics.nameDe: Cornelius Nepos: De viris illustribus (z. B. Hannibal)
topics.description: Read biographies by Cornelius Nepos, for example of Hannibal or Themistocles, and examine how ancient biography presents a life as a moral example (exemplum) and how it judges Rome's enemies.
evidence: Translate passages of a Nepos biography
Describe how Nepos characterises his hero through actions and judgements
Explain the function of the exemplum in Roman thinking
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain how Nepos presents Hannibal and whether he admires or condemns him?

prerequisites.reason: Nepos is one of the first unadapted authors
The Punic Wars are the background of the Hannibal life

topics.laenderNotes: Bayern Jgst. 9; Niedersachsen Kl. 10; BW Kl. 9/10 as one author to choose.

topics.subject: Latein
topics.name: Caesar: The Gallic War
topics.description: Read passages of Caesar's commentarii on the Gallic War (e.g. the Helvetians, Ariovistus, the excursus on Gauls and Germani, Vercingetorix) and analyse his clear style, third-person self-presentation and political purpose.
evidence: Translate Caesar passages including oratio obliqua and ablatives absolute
Show how Caesar presents himself and his opponents to justify the war
Evaluate the Germani excursus as an ethnographic and political text
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why Caesar writes about himself in the third person and what effect that has on readers in Rome?

prerequisites.reason: Caesar follows the transition to original texts
Caesar's style relies heavily on participle constructions
Caesar's political career frames the work

osMatches.note: os: Roman army and Caesar's raids on Britain

topics.laenderNotes: Bayern Jgst. 9 (Macht und Politik, with Nepos); BW Kl. 9/10 as one historical-political author to choose; NRW sample plan Kl. 10; Niedersachsen Kl. 10. Some plans now start with Ovid, Nepos or medieval Latin instead.

topics.subject: Latein
topics.name: Ovid: Metamorphoses
topics.description: Read myths from Ovid's Metamorphoses (e.g. Daedalus and Icarus, Pyramus and Thisbe, Apollo and Daphne, Niobe, Orpheus) in hexameters, interpret the motif of transformation and Ovid's narrative art, and follow the myths into later art and literature.
evidence: Translate and scan passages of a Metamorphoses episode
Interpret how the transformation reflects the character's nature or fate
Compare Ovid's version of a myth with a painting, sculpture or modern adaptation
topics.assessmentPrompt: After reading Daedalus and Icarus, can {{name}} explain what the story says about human ambition and how a painter like Bruegel took it up?

prerequisites.reason: The Metamorphoses are written in hexameters
Greek and Roman myths are known from the first years

topics.laenderNotes: Bayern: Ars amatoria Jgst. 10, Metamorphoses Jgst. 11; NRW Abitur 2029 (Grund- and Leistungskurs) includes the Metamorphoses; in BW Ovid is one poetic author to choose in Kl. 9/10.

topics.subject: Latein
topics.name: Catullus: Love Poetry
topics.description: Read poems by Catullus, especially the Lesbia cycle (e.g. carmina 5, 8, 85, 101), and interpret the personal voice of neoteric poetry, the conflict of love and hate, and its metres (hendecasyllable, elegiac couplet).
evidence: Translate and scan a short Catullus poem
Interpret the speaker's feelings and their development in the Lesbia poems
Compare a Catullus poem with a modern love poem or song
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain how the two lines of 'Odi et amo' (c. 85) express a contradiction in feelings?

prerequisites.reason: Many Catullus poems are in elegiac couplets
Interpretation relies on stylistic analysis

topics.laenderNotes: Bayern Jgst. 10 (Liebe und Leidenschaft) and again Jgst. 12; BW Kl. 9/10 as one poetic author to choose; NRW sample plan Kl. 10.

topics.subject: Latein
topics.name: Cicero's Speeches and Roman Rhetoric
topics.nameDe: Cicero: Reden (z. B. In Catilinam) und römische Rhetorik
topics.description: Read passages of Cicero's speeches (e.g. the Catilinarians or Verrines), analyse their structure (exordium, narratio, argumentatio, peroratio) and means of persuasion (logos, ethos, pathos), and judge rhetoric as a political instrument in the late Republic.
evidence: Identify the parts of a speech and their function
Analyse how Cicero uses stylistic devices and emotional appeals to sway his audience
Evaluate the speech as political propaganda in its historical situation
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} show how Cicero's opening 'Quo usque tandem…' attacks Catiline and why it is so effective?

prerequisites.reason: Rhetorical analysis builds on stylistic devices
The crisis of the Republic is the background

externalPrerequisites.subject: Deutsch
externalPrerequisites.reason: Speech analysis is also taught in German

topics.laenderNotes: Bayern reads Cicero court speeches in Jgst. 10 and the Philippics/Catilinarians in Jgst. 11; NRW (Q-phase) has antique rhetoric as a focus in Grund- and Leistungskurs.

topics.subject: Latein
topics.name: Cicero's Political Philosophy
topics.nameDe: Cicero: Staatsphilosophie (De re publica, De officiis)
topics.description: Read Cicero's philosophical writings on the state, such as De re publica (the mixed constitution, the Somnium Scipionis) or De officiis, and compare his idea of the best state and the duties of a citizen with Greek models and modern democracy.
evidence: Explain Cicero's definition of res publica and of the mixed constitution
Relate the text to Plato or Aristotle and to the Roman political crisis
Compare Cicero's ideas with principles of the Grundgesetz or modern democracy
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why Cicero thought a mix of monarchy, aristocracy and democracy was the best constitution?

prerequisites.reason: Cicero's political career is known from his speeches
Requires knowledge of the institutions of the Republic
Philosophical texts require interpretation skills

topics.laenderNotes: Bayern Jgst. 13 (Res publica res populi); NRW Abitur 2029: Cicero, De officiis in Grund- and Leistungskurs.

topics.subject: Latein
topics.name: Vergil: The Aeneid
topics.description: Read key passages of Vergil's Aeneid (e.g. the proem, Dido in Book 4, the underworld and the Heldenschau in Book 6) and interpret Aeneas' pietas, fate (fatum) and the poem's role as a founding myth for Augustan Rome.
evidence: Translate and scan passages of the Aeneid
Interpret the conflict between personal feelings and duty in the Dido episode
Explain how the epic legitimises Augustus' rule
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why Aeneas leaves Dido and how Vergil makes readers both understand and question his decision?

prerequisites.reason: Epic hexameter is known from Ovid
The Aeneas legend is known from the founding myths
The Augustan context is essential for interpretation

topics.laenderNotes: Bayern Jgst. 13 for all courses (Imperium sine fine dedi); in NRW the Aeneid (Book 4) is set only for the Leistungskurs in the Abitur 2029.

topics.subject: Latein
topics.name: Seneca: Letters on Ethics
topics.description: Read Seneca's letters to Lucilius (e.g. on the use of time, on slaves in letter 47, on death and fortune) and discuss their Stoic answers to questions of a good life and their relevance today.
evidence: Summarise and translate the argument of a Seneca letter
Explain the Stoic concepts used (virtus, ratio, sapiens, adiaphora)
Discuss whether Seneca's advice convinces a modern reader
topics.assessmentPrompt: After reading Seneca's first letter, can {{name}} explain what he means by 'vindica te tibi' and whether they agree?

prerequisites.reason: The letters apply Stoic doctrine
Requires interpretation of argumentative texts

topics.laenderNotes: Bayern Jgst. 12 (Philosophandum est); NRW Abitur 2029 Grund- and Leistungskurs; BW Kl. 11 as a philosophical author to choose.

topics.subject: Latein
topics.name: Roman Historiography: Sallust and Livy
topics.description: Read Roman historians, especially Sallust's monograph on Catiline's conspiracy and passages of Livy's Ab urbe condita, and analyse how they explain history through moral decline (ambitio, avaritia) or exemplary figures, with their typical style (Sallust's brevity, Livy's dramatic narration).
evidence: Translate passages of Sallust or Livy, including their characteristic style features
Explain Sallust's theory of moral decline after the fall of Carthage or Livy's use of exempla
Compare a historian’s portrait of a figure (e.g. Catiline) with another source and evaluate both
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} compare how Sallust and Cicero portray Catiline and explain why they differ?

prerequisites.reason: The comparison with Cicero's Catilinarians is central
Requires independent interpretation of difficult prose

osMatches.note: os: fall of the Roman Republic as history content

topics.laenderNotes: Bayern reads Sallust's Catilina in Jgst. 11 (Politik in Krisenzeiten); NRW Abitur 2029 sets Livy's first decade; BW offers Livy as a historical author in Kl. 11.

topics.subject: Latein
topics.name: Daily Life in Ancient Rome
topics.nameDe: Römischer Alltag: familia, domus, Schule, Thermen, Forum
topics.description: Know how people lived in ancient Rome as presented in the first textbook stories: the familia and the role of the pater familias, women and children, houses (domus, insula, villa), school, meals, baths, games and the forum.
evidence: Describe a Roman family and the roles of its members, including slaves
Compare a domus and an insula and explain who lived where
Describe places of public life (forum, thermae, circus, amphitheatrum) and what happened there
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell you what a Roman boy's day might have looked like and how it differs from their own?

prerequisites.reason: Roman daily life is introduced in Geschichte

osMatches.note: os: daily life in a Roman town (age 7–9); here linked to Latin texts

topics.subject: Latein
topics.name: Roman Society and Slavery
topics.nameDe: Römische Gesellschaft: Patrizier, Plebejer, Klientel, Sklaven
topics.description: Understand the structure of Roman society: patricians and plebeians, patronus and cliens, citizens and non-citizens, slaves and freedmen, and how these relationships appear in Latin texts.
evidence: Explain the patron–client relationship and its obligations
Describe the situation of slaves and how they could be freed
Identify social roles of characters in a Latin text
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why a Roman cliens visited his patronus every morning?

prerequisites.reason: Builds on the picture of the Roman familia
Patricians and plebeians are introduced in Geschichte

osMatches.note: os: Roman Republic including patricians and plebeians

topics.subject: Latein
topics.name: Gods, Myths and Roman Religion
topics.description: Know the Greek and Roman gods (Jupiter/Zeus, Juno/Hera, Minerva/Athena…), central myths and heroes (Troy, Ulixes/Odysseus, Hercules) and the practice of Roman religion: pietas, sacrifice, household gods (Lares, Penates), priests and omens.
evidence: Match Roman and Greek names of the main gods and their attributes
Retell a central myth or heroic legend from a Latin text
Describe Roman religious practice and the idea of do ut des
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell you the Greek name of Minerva, what she stands for, and how Romans tried to win the gods' favour?

prerequisites.reason: The Greek gods are introduced in Geschichte
Ancient legends are read in Deutsch

osMatches.note: os: Greek gods with Roman names (age 7–9)

topics.subject: Latein
topics.name: Rome's Founding Legends
topics.nameDe: Gründungssagen Roms: Aeneas, Romulus und Remus, Königszeit
topics.description: Know the legends of Rome's beginnings (Aeneas' flight from Troy, Romulus and Remus, the kings, Lucretia and the founding of the Republic) and understand how Romans used these stories to explain their values and institutions.
evidence: Retell the founding legend from Aeneas to Romulus
Explain what the legend of Lucretia was meant to justify
Distinguish legend from historical evidence (archaeology, dates)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell the story of Romulus and Remus and explain why the Romans liked to say they descended from Mars?

prerequisites.reason: The legends link Rome to Greek myth and the gods
The founding legend is first met in Geschichte

topics.subject: Latein
topics.name: The Roman Republic and Its Expansion
topics.nameDe: Römische Republik: Ämter, Senat und Expansion (Punische Kriege)
topics.description: Understand how the Roman Republic was governed (consuls and other magistrates, senate, assemblies, the cursus honorum) and how Rome expanded across Italy and the Mediterranean, especially in the wars against Carthage and Hannibal.
evidence: Describe the cursus honorum and the principles of annuity and collegiality
Explain the roles of senate, magistrates and popular assemblies
Outline the Punic Wars and their consequences for Rome
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why Rome always had two consuls who changed every year?

prerequisites.reason: The Republic begins after the expulsion of the kings
The Republic is introduced in Geschichte

osMatches.note: os: Roman Republic and Empire (age 9–11)

topics.subject: Latein
topics.name: Fall of the Republic and the Principate
topics.nameDe: Krise der Republik, Caesar und Augustus: das Prinzipat
topics.description: Trace the crisis of the late Republic (Gracchi, civil wars, Caesar's dictatorship) and Augustus' Principate, which kept republican forms while concentrating power, and see how authors of the period reflect it.
evidence: Outline the main stages from the Gracchi to Caesar's murder
Explain how Augustus secured power while claiming to restore the Republic
Relate an author (Caesar, Cicero, Vergil) to this political situation
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why Augustus called himself 'princeps' rather than king?

prerequisites.reason: The crisis can only be understood against the republican order
The imperial period is introduced in Geschichte

osMatches.note: os: fall of the Roman Republic (age 12–14)

topics.subject: Latein
topics.name: Romans in Germania
topics.nameDe: Römer in Germanien: Limes, Varusschlacht, Römerstädte
topics.description: Know how the Romans shaped the area of today's Germany: the provinces on Rhine and Danube, the Limes, the battle in the Teutoburg Forest, Roman towns such as Cologne, Trier, Mainz, Augsburg and Regensburg, and traces of Romanisation still visible today.
evidence: Locate Roman provinces, the Limes and Roman towns on a map of Germany
Read a Latin inscription or text about Romans and Germani
Find Roman traces in their own region (museum, place names, loanwords)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} name a Roman town in Germany, say what its Latin name was, and point to the Limes on a map?

prerequisites.reason: Limes and Varus battle are introduced in Geschichte
Romanisation is introduced in Geschichte
Expansion explains how Rome reached the Rhine

topics.laenderNotes: BW: life in the provinces and the Limes in Kl. 9/10; NRW: provinces in the first stage; Bayern links Roman traces to the local area (e.g. Augsburg, Regensburg).

topics.subject: Latein
topics.name: Roman Values
topics.nameDe: Römische Wertbegriffe (mos maiorum, virtus, pietas, fides, dignitas)
topics.description: Understand the central Roman values that cannot be translated by a single German word (mos maiorum, virtus, pietas, fides, dignitas, gloria, otium/negotium, humanitas) and use them to interpret texts and figures.
evidence: Explain the range of meaning of virtus, pietas and fides with examples
Identify value terms in a Latin text and explain their function
Compare a Roman value with a modern concept (e.g. pietas and loyalty)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why 'pius Aeneas' means more than 'der fromme Aeneas'?

prerequisites.reason: Exemplary figures of early Rome embody these values
Value terms are part of the core vocabulary

topics.subject: Latein
topics.name: Stoics and Epicureans
topics.description: Know the main ideas of the two philosophical schools most present in Latin texts: the Stoa (virtue, reason, living according to nature, apatheia) and Epicureanism (pleasure as absence of pain, fear of death and gods), and how Romans adapted Greek philosophy.
evidence: Explain the Stoic and Epicurean ideas of happiness
Identify Stoic or Epicurean arguments in a Latin text
Compare an ancient position with a modern answer to the same question
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain how a Stoic and an Epicurean would each answer the question 'What makes life happy?'

prerequisites.reason: Roman values are linked to philosophical concepts
Philosophy is contrasted with traditional religion

externalPrerequisites.subject: Religion & Ethik
externalPrerequisites.concept: Hellenistic ethics: Stoa and Epicurus on the good life
externalPrerequisites.reason: Philosophie/Ethik lessons may treat the same schools

topics.laenderNotes: NRW already introduces the basics of Stoa and Epicureanism in the second Sek I stage; Bayern Jgst. 12, BW Kl. 11 with Cicero or Seneca.

topics.subject: Latein
topics.name: Reception of Antiquity
topics.nameDe: Antikerezeption in Kunst, Literatur, Politik und Medien
topics.description: Investigate how Latin texts and Roman culture live on: Latin as the language of the Church, science and humanism, ancient myths in painting, sculpture and literature, Roman models in architecture and political language, and antiquity in film, comics and advertising.
evidence: Compare a Latin text with a later work of art or literature based on it
Explain why Latin remained a European lingua franca into the modern period
Analyse how a film, comic or advert uses ancient motifs and for what purpose
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} compare Ovid's story of Apollo and Daphne with Bernini's sculpture and say which moment each chooses?

prerequisites.reason: Ovid's myths are the most received Latin texts
The afterlife of Latin as a language was introduced earlier

externalPrerequisites.subject: Kunst
externalPrerequisites.reason: Art history supplies the visual examples

osMatches.note: os: Greek and Roman legacy today (age 9–11)

topics.subject: Französisch
topics.name: The French Republic and Its Values
topics.nameDe: La République: Institutionen, Werte und Zentralismus
topics.description: Understand how France is governed and how it sees itself: the Fifth Republic with its strong president, centralism and the role of Paris, the values liberté, égalité, fraternité and laïcité, the 14 juillet, and how these compare with Germany's federal system.
evidence: Describe the roles of president, prime minister and parliament in the Fifth Republic
Explain centralism and compare it with German federalism
Explain what laïcité means and discuss a current debate about it
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain in French why the French president has more power than the German chancellor and what 'laïcité' means at school?

prerequisites.reason: Comparing France and Germany builds on Franco-German topics
The régions show the administrative structure of France
Political debates are followed through press texts

externalPrerequisites.subject: Politik und Wirtschaft
externalPrerequisites.concept: federal system and constitutional organs of Germany
externalPrerequisites.reason: The German system is the point of comparison

topics.laenderNotes: Bayern: the 14 juillet in Jgst. 10, institutions of the Fifth Republic and centralism in the Oberstufe; BW: French politics (e.g. the president) in Kl. 11; NRW Q-phase theme Défis et visions de l'avenir (values and understanding of democracy).

topics.subject: Latein
topics.name: Evaluating Published Translations
topics.description: Compare several published German translations of the same Latin passage with the original and with each other, describe the translation strategies they follow (faithful, modernising, poetic) and reach a reasoned judgement on how well each renders content, structure and style.
evidence: Identify where two published translations differ and trace each difference back to the Latin
Name the translation strategy behind each version (e.g. literal, modernising, verse translation)
Write a reasoned evaluation of which translation best serves a given purpose
topics.assessmentPrompt: Given two German translations of a Vergil passage, can {{name}} show with the Latin text which one keeps the word order and imagery better and justify a preference?

prerequisites.reason: Judging translations requires translating well oneself
Evaluation depends on understanding the original's message and style

topics.laenderNotes: The KMK EPA lists the reasoned comparison of translations under the Leistungskurs; NRW (first Sek I stage) and BW (Kl. 11) already practise simpler translation comparisons with all students.

topics.subject: Latein
topics.name: Rome's Self-Image and Its Critics
topics.nameDe: Romidee und Romkritik: Rom und die Fremden
topics.description: Analyse how Latin authors justify Roman rule as a civilising mission (Vergil's 'tu regere imperio populos…', Livy) and how critical voices answer it, such as the speech of Calgacus in Tacitus ('ubi solitudinem faciunt, pacem appellant') or Caesar's portrayal of Gauls and Germani, and relate this to modern debates on empire.
evidence: Explain the Roman mission as presented in Vergil or Livy, with Latin quotations
Analyse a critical text on Roman rule and its arguments
Discuss how Rome's attitude to foreign peoples is judged from today's perspective
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} contrast Anchises' words on Rome's mission in Aeneid 6 with Calgacus' speech in Tacitus and say which arguments convince them?

prerequisites.reason: Vergil's Aeneid is the key text of the Roman mission
Augustan ideology is the background
Caesar's portrayal of foreign peoples is an earlier example

externalPrerequisites.subject: Geschichte
externalPrerequisites.reason: Modern comparisons draw on history lessons

topics.laenderNotes: The EPA names Rome's attitude to foreigners for both course levels; the new NRW Sek II plan (2026) lists 'Romidee und Romkritik' only for the Leistungskurs, and the Bayern Oberstufe treats it within the Augustan literature (Jgst. 13).

clusters.subject: Französisch
clusters.summary: In the first year of French your child is learning how French sounds and is spelt: silent letters, nasal vowels, liaison and the accents.
clusters.summaryDe: Im ersten Lernjahr Französisch lernt Ihr Kind, wie Französisch klingt und geschrieben wird: stumme Buchstaben, Nasalvokale, Liaison und Akzente.

clusters.subject: Französisch
clusters.summary: Your child is learning the basics of French grammar: articles and gender, être and avoir, the present tense of the main verb groups, negation, questions, adjectives and the near future.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt die Grundlagen der französischen Grammatik: Artikel und Genus, être und avoir, das Präsens der wichtigsten Verbgruppen, Verneinung, Fragen, Adjektive und das futur composé.

clusters.subject: Französisch
clusters.summary: Your child is learning to talk about the past with the passé composé and the imparfait, to use object pronouns, the partitive article and relative clauses.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt, mit passé composé und imparfait über Vergangenes zu sprechen, und verwendet Objektpronomen, den Teilungsartikel und Relativsätze.

clusters.subject: Französisch
clusters.summary: Your child is learning the more demanding structures: futur simple, conditionnel and if-clauses, the subjonctif, reported speech, the gérondif and recognising the literary passé simple.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt anspruchsvollere Strukturen: futur simple, conditionnel und si-Sätze, den subjonctif, die indirekte Rede, das gérondif und das Erkennen des literarischen passé simple.

clusters.subject: Französisch
clusters.summary: Your child is learning first French words for numbers, the time, school and the daily routine.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt erste französische Wörter für Zahlen, Uhrzeit, Schule und Tagesablauf.

clusters.subject: Französisch
clusters.summary: Your child is building vocabulary for food and shopping, hobbies, media, holidays and travel.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind baut Wortschatz zu Essen und Einkaufen, Hobbys, Medien, Ferien und Reisen auf.

clusters.subject: Französisch
clusters.summary: Your child is learning to greet people, introduce themselves and their family in French, and to keep talking when a word is missing.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt, auf Französisch zu grüßen, sich und die Familie vorzustellen und weiterzusprechen, wenn ein Wort fehlt.

clusters.subject: Französisch
clusters.summary: Your child is learning to manage everyday situations in France, such as shopping, ordering or asking the way, and to give a short prepared talk.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt, Alltagssituationen in Frankreich zu bewältigen (einkaufen, bestellen, nach dem Weg fragen) und einen kurzen vorbereiteten Vortrag zu halten.

clusters.subject: Französisch
clusters.summary: Your child is learning to give and justify opinions in French and to take part in discussions.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt, auf Französisch Meinungen zu äußern, zu begründen und an Diskussionen teilzunehmen.

clusters.subject: Französisch
clusters.summary: In the Oberstufe your teenager presents texts and pictures in French and defends a position, as required in the oral exam.
clusters.summaryDe: In der Oberstufe stellt Ihr Kind Texte und Bilder auf Französisch vor und vertritt eine eigene Position, wie es die mündliche Prüfung verlangt.

clusters.subject: Französisch
clusters.summary: Your child is learning to understand classroom French, short dialogues and announcements, listening for the gist or for details.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt, Unterrichtsfranzösisch, kurze Dialoge und Durchsagen zu verstehen, global oder auf Einzelheiten hin.

clusters.subject: Französisch
clusters.summary: Your child is learning to understand French songs, video clips and short films.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt, französische Chansons, Videoclips und Kurzfilme zu verstehen.

clusters.subject: Französisch
clusters.summary: Your teenager is learning to follow authentic French radio, podcasts, news and films, including regional and francophone accents in the Leistungskurs.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt, authentisches französisches Radio, Podcasts, Nachrichten und Filme zu verstehen, im Leistungskurs auch regionale und frankophone Akzente.

clusters.subject: Französisch
clusters.summary: Your child is learning to read short French texts such as messages, programmes and simple factual texts.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt, kurze französische Texte wie Nachrichten, Programme und einfache Sachtexte zu lesen.

clusters.subject: Französisch
clusters.summary: Your child is reading a longer French youth novel and following its plot and characters.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind liest einen längeren französischen Jugendroman und verfolgt Handlung und Figuren.

clusters.subject: Französisch
clusters.summary: Your teenager is learning to read French newspaper articles and editorials and to recognise the author's intention.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt, französische Zeitungsartikel und Kommentare zu lesen und die Absicht des Autors zu erkennen.

clusters.subject: Französisch
clusters.summary: Your child is learning to write short messages and e-mails to a French pen friend.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt, kurze Nachrichten und E-Mails an eine französische Brieffreundin oder einen Brieffreund zu schreiben.

clusters.subject: Französisch
clusters.summary: Your child is learning to write about experiences and short stories in French, using the past tenses.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt, auf Französisch über Erlebnisse zu schreiben und kurze Geschichten zu erzählen, mit den Vergangenheitszeiten.

clusters.subject: Französisch
clusters.summary: Your child is learning to write opinion texts and formal letters, for example an application for a holiday job.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt, Stellungnahmen und formelle Briefe zu schreiben, zum Beispiel eine Bewerbung um einen Ferienjob.

clusters.subject: Französisch
clusters.summary: Your teenager is practising the Abitur text types: résumé, argumentative commentary and creative writing; the Leistungskurs also adapts texts for new readers.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind übt die Abitur-Textsorten: Résumé, argumentativer Kommentar und kreatives Schreiben; im Leistungskurs auch das Umgestalten von Texten für neue Adressaten.

clusters.subject: Französisch
clusters.summary: Your child is learning to help others in everyday situations by passing on the gist between French and German.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt, in Alltagssituationen zu helfen, indem es das Wesentliche zwischen Französisch und Deutsch vermittelt.

clusters.subject: Französisch
clusters.summary: Your child is learning to convey the key points of a German text in French for a French reader, a task that is part of many Abitur exams.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt, die wichtigsten Inhalte eines deutschen Textes für französische Leser auf Französisch wiederzugeben, eine Aufgabe vieler Abiturprüfungen.

clusters.subject: Französisch
clusters.summary: In the Leistungskurs your teenager adds the explanations a French reader needs to understand German realities.
clusters.summaryDe: Im Leistungskurs ergänzt Ihr Kind die Erklärungen, die französische Leser brauchen, um deutsche Gegebenheiten zu verstehen.

clusters.subject: Französisch
clusters.summary: Your child is discovering everyday life and school in France and first sights of Paris.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind entdeckt Alltag und Schule in Frankreich und erste Sehenswürdigkeiten von Paris.

clusters.subject: Französisch
clusters.summary: Your child is getting to know the regions of France and the francophone world, from Québec to West Africa.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt die Regionen Frankreichs und die frankophone Welt von Québec bis Westafrika kennen.

clusters.subject: Französisch
clusters.summary: Your child is learning how Germany and France became partners and what the Élysée Treaty means for exchanges today.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt, wie Deutschland und Frankreich zu Partnern wurden und was der Élysée-Vertrag heute für Austausche bedeutet.

clusters.subject: Französisch
clusters.summary: Your teenager is studying French society: cities and banlieues, migration, the colonial past and the institutions and values of the Republic.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind beschäftigt sich mit der französischen Gesellschaft: Städte und Banlieues, Migration, die koloniale Vergangenheit sowie Institutionen und Werte der Republik.

clusters.subject: Französisch
clusters.summary: Your child is learning to read French comics (bandes dessinées) and how pictures and text work together.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt, französische Comics (bandes dessinées) zu lesen und das Zusammenspiel von Bild und Text zu deuten.

clusters.subject: Französisch
clusters.summary: Your teenager is analysing French stories, poems, songs, films and non-fiction texts; the Leistungskurs also interprets texts in their historical context.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind analysiert französische Erzähltexte, Gedichte, Chansons, Filme und Sachtexte; im Leistungskurs auch Texte in ihrem historischen Kontext.

clusters.subject: Französisch
clusters.summary: Your child is learning how to learn French vocabulary and how to use English, German and Latin to guess new words.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt, wie man französische Vokabeln lernt und wie Englisch, Deutsch und Latein beim Erschließen neuer Wörter helfen.

clusters.subject: Französisch
clusters.summary: Your child is learning to use dictionaries, to assess their own level and, if they wish, to prepare for the DELF certificate.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt, Wörterbücher zu nutzen, das eigene Niveau einzuschätzen und sich auf Wunsch auf das DELF-Zertifikat vorzubereiten.

clusters.subject: Französisch
clusters.summary: Your teenager is learning to tell informal, standard and formal French apart and to choose the right register.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt, umgangssprachliches, standardsprachliches und gehobenes Französisch zu unterscheiden und das passende Register zu wählen.

clusters.subject: Latein
clusters.summary: In the first year of Latin your child is learning to read Latin aloud and to see how differently Latin and German build sentences.
clusters.summaryDe: Im ersten Lernjahr Latein lernt Ihr Kind, Latein vorzulesen, und sieht, wie unterschiedlich Latein und Deutsch Sätze bauen.

clusters.subject: Latein
clusters.summary: Your child is discovering Latin words in German, English and the Romance languages.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind entdeckt lateinische Wörter im Deutschen, Englischen und in den romanischen Sprachen.

clusters.subject: Latein
clusters.summary: Your child is learning Latin vocabulary together with its learning forms, such as genitive, gender and principal parts.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt lateinische Vokabeln mit ihren Lernformen wie Genitiv, Genus und Stammformen.

clusters.subject: Latein
clusters.summary: Your child is learning to work out unknown Latin words from prefixes, suffixes and word families.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt, unbekannte lateinische Wörter über Präfixe, Suffixe und Wortfamilien zu erschließen.

clusters.subject: Latein
clusters.summary: Your child is learning to use a Latin dictionary and to choose the meaning that fits the context.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt, ein lateinisches Wörterbuch zu benutzen und die passende Bedeutung im Kontext zu wählen.

clusters.subject: Latein
clusters.summary: Your child is learning the first declensions and conjugations, the tenses of the indicative and the main pronouns.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt die ersten Deklinationen und Konjugationen, die Tempora des Indikativs und die wichtigsten Pronomen.

clusters.subject: Latein
clusters.summary: Your child is learning the passive, the subjunctive forms, the remaining declensions, comparison and the irregular verbs.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt das Passiv, die Konjunktivformen, die übrigen Deklinationen, die Steigerung und die unregelmäßigen Verben.

clusters.subject: Latein
clusters.summary: Your child is learning the deponent verbs, which look passive but have an active meaning.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt die Deponentien kennen, die passiv aussehen, aber aktiv übersetzt werden.

clusters.subject: Latein
clusters.summary: Your child is learning to analyse Latin sentences: sentence elements, the functions of the ablative, subordinate clauses and the AcI.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt, lateinische Sätze zu analysieren: Satzglieder, Ablativfunktionen, Gliedsätze und den AcI.

clusters.subject: Latein
clusters.summary: Your child is learning the typical Latin constructions: participles (participium coniunctum, ablativus absolutus), subjunctive clauses and the sequence of tenses.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt die typischen lateinischen Konstruktionen: Partizipien (participium coniunctum, ablativus absolutus), konjunktivische Gliedsätze und die consecutio temporum.

clusters.subject: Latein
clusters.summary: Your child is completing Latin grammar with the subjunctive in main clauses, the gerund and gerundive and indirect speech.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind schließt die lateinische Grammatik mit dem Konjunktiv im Hauptsatz, Gerundium und Gerundivum sowie der indirekten Rede ab.

clusters.subject: Latein
clusters.summary: Your child is learning methods to decode a Latin sentence step by step before translating it.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt Methoden, einen lateinischen Satz Schritt für Schritt zu erschließen, bevor es ihn übersetzt.

clusters.subject: Latein
clusters.summary: Your child is learning to grasp a whole text before translating and to turn a literal translation into good German.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt, einen Text vor dem Übersetzen als Ganzes zu erfassen und eine wörtliche Übersetzung in gutes Deutsch zu bringen.

clusters.subject: Latein
clusters.summary: Your child is learning stylistic devices and metre (hexameter, elegiac couplet) and works towards the Latinum level of translation.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt Stilmittel und Metrik (Hexameter, Distichon) und arbeitet auf das Übersetzungsniveau des Latinums hin.

clusters.subject: Latein
clusters.summary: Your teenager is learning to interpret Latin texts in their context; the Leistungskurs also compares and evaluates published translations.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt, lateinische Texte in ihrem Kontext zu interpretieren; im Leistungskurs werden auch veröffentlichte Übersetzungen verglichen und bewertet.

clusters.subject: Latein
clusters.summary: Your child is moving from the textbook to real Latin authors such as Nepos, Caesar, Ovid and Catullus.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind wechselt vom Lehrbuch zu echten lateinischen Autoren wie Nepos, Caesar, Ovid und Catull.

clusters.subject: Latein
clusters.summary: Your teenager is reading the major authors of the Abitur: Cicero, Sallust and Livy, Seneca and Vergil.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind liest die großen Autoren des Abiturs: Cicero, Sallust und Livius, Seneca und Vergil.

clusters.subject: Latein
clusters.summary: Your child is learning about daily life, society, gods and myths in ancient Rome through the textbook stories.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt über die Lehrbuchtexte Alltag, Gesellschaft, Götter und Mythen im antiken Rom kennen.

clusters.subject: Latein
clusters.summary: Your child is learning Rome's history from its founding legends through the Republic to Augustus, and the Romans' traces in Germany.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt die Geschichte Roms von den Gründungssagen über die Republik bis zu Augustus und die Spuren der Römer in Deutschland kennen.

clusters.subject: Latein
clusters.summary: Your child is learning the Roman values such as virtus, pietas and fides that explain how the authors think.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt römische Wertbegriffe wie virtus, pietas und fides, die das Denken der Autoren erklären.

clusters.subject: Latein
clusters.summary: Your teenager is studying ancient philosophy, the afterlife of antiquity in art and culture and, in the Leistungskurs, Rome's self-image and its critics.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind beschäftigt sich mit antiker Philosophie, dem Fortwirken der Antike in Kunst und Kultur und im Leistungskurs mit Romidee und Romkritik.
